lessons.title: From company teams to Club Necaxa
lessons.subtitle: A Mexico City club built from the Luz y Fuerza and Tranvías teams.

story.title: An August founding
story.body: The club traces its founding to 21 August 1923 in Mexico City. William H. Fraser brought together players from the Luz y Fuerza and Tranvías company teams.

story.title: Early identity
story.body: Necaxa’s first league campaign ended fifth. It won its first Copa Eliminatoria in 1924/25 and adopted the nickname Electricistas the following season.

facts.label: Necaxa founding date
facts.prompt: On what date does Necaxa mark its founding?
facts.scope: Official club founding date.
facts.evidence: The club history gives 21 August 1923 as the founding date in Mexico City.

facts.label: Organizer of Necaxa’s founding
facts.prompt: Who does Necaxa name as the organizer who brought the Luz y Fuerza and Tranvías teams together in 1923?
facts.scope: Club origin account.
facts.evidence: Necaxa credits engineer William H. Fraser with bringing together the company teams.

facts.label: Necaxa’s first Copa Eliminatoria
facts.prompt: In which season does Necaxa say it won its first Copa Eliminatoria?
facts.scope: First club trophy listed in its official history.
facts.evidence: The club says it won its first cup in the 1924–25 campaign.

lessons.title: Necaxa’s Campeonísimo era
lessons.subtitle: A five-title campaign and two later league crowns

story.title: A landmark season
story.body: Necaxa’s official history describes the 1934–35 campaign as an extraordinary five-title year across league, cup, district, national and Central American competitions.

story.title: A lasting side
story.body: The club also records league championships in 1936–37 and 1937–38. Its historical account names Horacio Casarín as a leading figure during those two seasons.

facts.label: Titles in the 1934–35 campaign
facts.prompt: How many titles does Necaxa say it won in the 1934–35 campaign?
facts.scope: 1932 league final, as described by the club.
facts.evidence: The club history lists league, cup, Distrito Federal, national and Central American titles for 1934–35.

facts.label: League title after 1934–35
facts.prompt: In which season did Necaxa win the league title after 1934–35?
facts.scope: Trophy count for the 1934–35 multi-competition season.
facts.evidence: Club history lists league titles in 1936–37 and 1937–38.

facts.label: League title after 1936–37
facts.prompt: Which later season did Necaxa win the league after 1936–37?
facts.scope: Club withdrawal, followed by an eight-year hiatus.
facts.evidence: Club history lists league titles in 1936–37 and 1937–38.

lessons.title: Necaxa returns to professional football
lessons.subtitle: The club re-entered the top flight in 1950.

story.title: Back in the league
story.body: After an eight-year absence, Necaxa returned under the sponsorship of the Electricians’ Union. Its first professional-era match was played in Guadalajara.

story.title: A goalless opening
story.body: Horacio Casarín led the side against Guadalajara at Parque Oblatos on 24 September 1950. The match finished 0–0.

facts.label: Professional-era return date
facts.prompt: On what date did Club Necaxa reappear in professional football in 1950?
facts.scope: Professional-era reappearance.
facts.evidence: The club dates its return to professional football to 24 September 1950.

facts.label: Opponent in Necaxa’s professional return
facts.prompt: Which club did Necaxa face in its first professional-era match on 24 September 1950?
facts.scope: First professional-era match.
facts.evidence: The club says its return match was against Guadalajara at Parque Oblatos.

facts.label: Score in Necaxa’s professional return
facts.prompt: What was the score in Necaxa’s 24 September 1950 professional-era return match against Guadalajara?
facts.scope: 24 September 1950 match result.
facts.evidence: The club records a goalless draw in the match.

lessons.title: A second Necaxa spell begins in Cuba
lessons.subtitle: A veteran forward rejoined when the club came back.

story.title: An abrupt change of plan
story.body: Horacio Casarín was in Cuba for Veracruz’s preseason when Necaxa returned to professional football. He ended his Veracruz contract and came back to the club for a second spell.

story.title: Back with the Electricistas
story.body: Necaxa’s retrospective places Casarín at the center of its return, with the forward leading the team on the field in its first professional-era match.

facts.label: Previous club
facts.prompt: Which club had Horacio Casarín joined for preseason in Cuba before returning to Necaxa in 1950?
facts.scope: Casarín’s return from Veracruz to Necaxa in 1950.
facts.evidence: Necaxa says Casarín was in preseason in Cuba with Veracruz before he returned.

facts.label: Contract decision
facts.prompt: What did Horacio Casarín do with his Veracruz contract to return to Necaxa in 1950?
facts.scope: Casarín’s return from Veracruz to Necaxa in 1950.
facts.evidence: Necaxa says Casarín rescinded his Veracruz contract to return.

facts.label: Return spell
facts.prompt: Was Horacio Casarín beginning his first or second Necaxa spell when he returned in 1950?
facts.scope: Casarín’s return from Veracruz to Necaxa in 1950.
facts.evidence: The club identifies his 1950 return as his second stage with Necaxa.

lessons.title: Casarín moves from Necaxa to Atlante
lessons.subtitle: His early title-era place was followed by a major move in 1942 and another league crown.

story.title: A debut at Necaxa
story.body: The Rayados historical archive places Horacio Casarín’s debut with Necaxa in 1936, during the club’s “Once Hermanos” era. It then traces his career to Atlante, where he continued to establish himself as a leading figure.

story.title: A new league title
story.body: Casarín joined Atlante in 1942 and became champion there in 1946–47. This career transition connects his early Necaxa years to his later club honors, rather than repeating Necaxa’s title-season chronology.

facts.label: Senior debut
facts.prompt: In what year does Rayados’ historical profile date Horacio Casarín’s debut with Necaxa?
facts.scope: Horacio Casarín’s senior debut with Necaxa, according to Monterrey’s historical profile.
facts.evidence: Rayados’ archive states that Casarín debuted in 1936 with Necaxa.

facts.label: Career move
facts.prompt: In what year does Rayados’ archive say Horacio Casarín was signed by Atlante?
facts.scope: Horacio Casarín’s move from Necaxa to Atlante, as described in Monterrey’s historical profile.
facts.evidence: The archive says Casarín was signed by Atlante in 1942.

facts.label: Atlante title
facts.prompt: Which season did Horacio Casarín win a league championship with Atlante?
facts.scope: Atlante league title season credited to Casarín in Monterrey’s historical profile.
facts.evidence: The Rayados article states that Casarín was champion with Atlante in 1946–47.

lessons.title: A scoring crown after returning
lessons.subtitle: A Necaxa scoring crown and a later first for Monterrey.

story.title: Top scorer after Necaxa’s return
story.body: After returning to Necaxa, Horacio Casarín won the Mexican professional league scoring title in 1950–51 with 19 goals. Necaxa’s records identify him as the first of the club’s professional-era scoring champions.

story.title: A later milestone
story.body: At age 38, Casarín joined Monterrey for 1956–57. The Rayados archive says his goal against Toluca on 29 July 1956 was the first goal Monterrey scored at Estadio Tecnológico in a top-flight match.

facts.label: Scoring-title season
facts.prompt: In which league season did Horacio Casarín win Necaxa’s first professional-era scoring title?
facts.scope: Casarín’s Necaxa scoring title in 1950–51.
facts.evidence: Necaxa dates Casarín’s top-scoring campaign to 1950–51.

facts.label: League-leading goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Horacio Casarín score for Necaxa in the 1950–51 league-leading campaign?
facts.scope: Casarín’s Necaxa scoring title in 1950–51.
facts.evidence: The club records 19 goals for Casarín in the 1950–51 scoring-title season.

facts.label: Rayados milestone
facts.prompt: Which club did Horacio Casarín score against when he recorded Monterrey’s first top-flight goal at Estadio Tecnológico on 29 July 1956?
facts.scope: Monterrey’s first top-flight goal at Estadio Tecnológico, scored by Casarín on 29 July 1956.
facts.evidence: CF Monterrey’s archive says Casarín opened the scoring against Toluca in Monterrey’s first top-flight game at Estadio Tecnológico; the goal was the stadium’s first first-division goal for Rayados.

lessons.title: Casarín scores against Switzerland at Brazil 1950
lessons.subtitle: Mexico’s final group match ended with a late goal from its center-forward.

story.title: A late consolation
story.body: On 2 July 1950, Mexico faced Switzerland in Porto Alegre. The DFB match record shows Switzerland leading 2–0 before Horacio Casarín scored Mexico’s only goal in the 89th minute.

story.title: A World Cup goal
story.body: The 2–1 result was Mexico’s last match of the tournament. Casarín’s late strike is distinct from his Necaxa league scoring title and marks his contribution on football’s largest international stage.

facts.label: Match date
facts.prompt: On what date did Horacio Casarín score for Mexico against Switzerland at the 1950 FIFA World Cup?
facts.scope: Mexico–Switzerland, 1950 FIFA World Cup group match, Porto Alegre.
facts.evidence: The DFB data-center match page dates Switzerland 2–1 Mexico to Sunday, 2 July 1950.

facts.label: Late goal
facts.prompt: In which minute did Horacio Casarín score Mexico’s goal against Switzerland in the 1950 World Cup?
facts.scope: Mexico–Switzerland, 1950 FIFA World Cup group match, Porto Alegre.
facts.evidence: The DFB event record assigns Casarín’s Mexico goal at 89 minutes.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the final score when Horacio Casarín scored for Mexico against Switzerland on 2 July 1950?
facts.scope: Mexico–Switzerland, 1950 FIFA World Cup group match, Porto Alegre.
facts.evidence: DFB’s match page records the final score as Switzerland 2–1 Mexico and names Casarín as Mexico’s 89th-minute scorer.

lessons.title: Basay plans a return to Chile
lessons.subtitle: A decade abroad before a return at 29

story.title: Years abroad
story.body: Ivo Basay said he had spent close to ten years playing outside Chile before returning home at 29.

story.title: A hoped-for destination
story.body: He wanted to end his playing career at Colo-Colo, the Chilean club he supported, after achieving major team and individual goals in Mexico.

facts.label: Years playing abroad
facts.prompt: For how long did Ivo Basay say he had played outside Chile before returning at age 29?
facts.scope: Basay’s self-reported return to Chile at age 29.
facts.evidence: Basay said he had played outside Chile for close to ten years.

facts.label: Return age
facts.prompt: At what age did Ivo Basay say he returned to Chile after playing abroad?
facts.scope: Basay’s self-reported return to Chile at age 29.
facts.evidence: Basay’s interview says he returned to Chile at 29.

facts.label: Career destination
facts.prompt: Which Chilean club did Ivo Basay say he hoped to represent at the end of his playing career?
facts.scope: Basay’s self-reported return to Chile at age 29.
facts.evidence: Basay says he wanted to finish at Colo-Colo, the club he supported.

lessons.title: Basay scores in Necaxa’s 1995 final
lessons.subtitle: He remembered the strike as the goal of his career.

story.title: A strike against Cruz Azul
story.body: On 4 June 1995, Ivo Basay scored Necaxa’s final goal in the league final against Cruz Azul.

story.title: A drought-ending finish
story.body: Basay recalled the strike as decisive because Necaxa had not won the league for 54 years; the long run of work had finally brought the championship.

facts.label: Final goal date
facts.prompt: On what date did Ivo Basay score his last Necaxa goal in the 1994–95 league final against Cruz Azul?
facts.scope: Necaxa–Cruz Azul 1994–95 league final, 4 June 1995.
facts.evidence: The club article dates Basay’s last Necaxa goal to 4 June 1995.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Ivo Basay score against in Necaxa’s 1994–95 league final?
facts.scope: Necaxa–Cruz Azul 1994–95 league final, 4 June 1995.
facts.evidence: The account places Basay’s final Necaxa goal in the final against Cruz Azul.

facts.label: Title drought
facts.prompt: How long had Necaxa gone without a league title before Ivo Basay’s 4 June 1995 final goal helped secure the championship?
facts.scope: Necaxa–Cruz Azul 1994–95 league final, 4 June 1995.
facts.evidence: Basay said the title ended a 54-year Necaxa league drought.

lessons.title: Basay’s club and international scoring totals
lessons.subtitle: His 27-goal Necaxa season sits alongside a separate national-team record.

story.title: A season at the top
story.body: Necaxa records 27 goals for Basay in the campaign when he became Mexico’s league top scorer.

story.title: A lasting Rayos total
story.body: Necaxa’s 2016 retrospective credits Basay with 99 goals for the club. La Roja’s national-team record lists six goals in 24 appearances for Chile, a separate international tally.

facts.label: League-leading goals
facts.prompt: How many league goals did Ivo Basay score for Necaxa in his league-leading Mexican season?
facts.scope: Basay’s Necaxa goal totals and scoring title.
facts.evidence: Necaxa records 27 goals for Basay when he won the league scoring title.

facts.label: Chile goals
facts.prompt: How many goals does La Roja credit Ivo Basay with scoring for Chile?
facts.scope: Ivo Basay’s senior Chile career, as listed by La Roja; six goals in 24 appearances.
facts.evidence: La Roja’s historical profile states Basay made 24 appearances for Chile and scored six goals.

facts.label: Club goal total
facts.prompt: How many goals does Necaxa’s 2016 Basay retrospective credit him with scoring for the club?
facts.scope: Necaxa retrospective published 15 July 2016; club goal total without a competition breakdown.
facts.evidence: The retrospective says Basay scored 99 times for Necaxa.

lessons.title: Basay opens his Chile scoring account
lessons.subtitle: Basay’s 1990s spell is tied to an important final.

story.title: A Lima comeback
story.body: Ivo Basay’s first Chile goal came against Peru in a 19 June 1987 friendly in Lima; Chile rallied from behind to win 3–1.

story.title: A national-team record
story.body: La Roja’s retrospective lists 24 appearances and six goals for Basay with Chile.

facts.label: First Chile goal date
facts.prompt: On what date did Ivo Basay score his first goal for Chile against Peru in Lima?
facts.scope: Chile–Peru friendly in Lima, 19 June 1987; Basay national-team record.
facts.evidence: La Roja dates the friendly to Friday 19 June 1987.

facts.label: Chile debut-goal match
facts.prompt: What was Chile’s score against Peru in Lima when Ivo Basay scored his first international goal on 19 June 1987?
facts.scope: Chile–Peru friendly in Lima, 19 June 1987; Basay national-team record.
facts.evidence: La Roja reports a 3–1 Chile victory over Peru.

facts.label: Chile appearances
facts.prompt: How many senior appearances does La Roja list for Ivo Basay?
facts.scope: Ivo Basay’s senior Chile career, as listed by La Roja.
facts.evidence: La Roja lists 24 appearances for Basay alongside his six international goals.

lessons.title: Gallos Blancos through the decades
lessons.subtitle: Querétaro’s official timeline tracks its rise and cup success.

story.title: A July beginning
story.body: The club dates its formal history to 8 July 1950. Its story includes promotion campaigns and a first Liga MX final in 2015.

story.title: A cup at home
story.body: In 2016 Querétaro lifted the Copa MX at Estadio Corregidora after beating Chivas.

facts.label: Querétaro founding date
facts.prompt: On what date does Querétaro mark the beginning of its history?
facts.scope: Club date of origin.
facts.evidence: The official timeline says the club’s formal history began 8 July 1950.

facts.label: Querétaro’s first Liga MX final
facts.prompt: In what year did Querétaro play its first Liga MX final?
facts.scope: First top-flight final.
facts.evidence: The club’s timeline identifies 2015 as its first Liga MX final.

facts.label: Querétaro’s 2016 cup
facts.prompt: Which cup did Querétaro win in 2016?
facts.scope: Club honor.
facts.evidence: The club says it lifted the Copa MX in 2016.

lessons.title: A comeback in the 2015 final
lessons.subtitle: Querétaro rallied in the return leg but fell short overall.

story.title: Three before halftime
story.body: In its first Liga MX final, Querétaro scored three times in the first half of the second leg against Santos.

story.title: A narrow turnaround
story.body: Ronaldinho entered around the hour mark, but Santos held on to win the Clausura 2015 final 5–3 on aggregate.

facts.label: Clausura 2015 final second-leg date
facts.prompt: On what date did Querétaro play the second leg of the Clausura 2015 Liga MX final against Santos Laguna?
facts.scope: Clausura 2015 final second leg.
facts.evidence: CONCACAF dates the return leg in Querétaro to 31 May 2015.

facts.label: Querétaro’s first-half goals in the final
facts.prompt: How many first-half goals did Querétaro score against Santos Laguna in the second leg of the Clausura 2015 Liga MX final?
facts.scope: Second leg of the final.
facts.evidence: The report says Querétaro scored three times before halftime.

facts.label: Clausura 2015 final aggregate
facts.prompt: What aggregate score did Santos Laguna post against Querétaro to win the Clausura 2015 Liga MX final?
facts.scope: Two-leg final aggregate.
facts.evidence: Santos retained the title with a 5–3 aggregate result.

lessons.title: The 2016 cup arrives at Corregidora
lessons.subtitle: The club’s history marks its first Copa MX triumph.

story.title: A first cup
story.body: Querétaro’s official timeline says it won its first Copa MX in 2016, at home.

story.title: A Guadalajara final
story.body: The club’s timeline identifies Chivas as the opponent defeated to lift the trophy.

facts.label: Copa MX victory year
facts.prompt: In which calendar year did Querétaro win the Copa MX final against Guadalajara?
facts.scope: Copa MX title year.
facts.evidence: The club lists its Copa MX win in 2016.

facts.label: Copa MX final stadium
facts.prompt: At which stadium did Querétaro play the 2016 Copa MX final against Guadalajara?
facts.scope: 2016 cup final venue.
facts.evidence: The club says it lifted the trophy at home at Estadio Corregidora.

facts.label: Copa MX final opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Querétaro defeat in the 2016 Copa MX final?
facts.scope: 2016 Copa MX final.
facts.evidence: The official history states Querétaro beat Chivas.

lessons.title: Ronaldinho’s rise from Brazil to Europe
lessons.subtitle: A youth world title preceded the senior team and a move to Paris.

story.title: Early international success
story.body: FIFA’s career retrospective traces Ronaldinho from Grêmio to Paris Saint-Germain. Before that European move, he helped Brazil win the FIFA U-17 World Cup in Egypt in 1997, then became part of the senior national team that won the 1999 Copa América.

story.title: The European step
story.body: Ronaldinho left Grêmio for PSG in 2001. He moved on to Barcelona in 2003, where he won two league titles and the Champions League. This lesson focuses on the early route into his senior career rather than repeating the Querétaro final.

facts.label: Youth international title
facts.prompt: Which FIFA youth tournament did Ronaldinho win with Brazil in Egypt in 1997?
distractors: FIFA U-17 World Cup in Peru
facts.scope: Brazil’s 1997 FIFA U-17 World Cup title; FIFA career retrospective.
facts.evidence: FIFA says Ronaldinho began to shine in Brazil’s victory at the 1997 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Egypt.

facts.label: Senior international honor
facts.prompt: Which senior national-team tournament did Ronaldinho win with Brazil in Paraguay in 1999?
facts.scope: Brazil senior team, Copa América Paraguay 1999.
facts.evidence: FIFA states that Ronaldinho joined Brazil’s senior team for its Copa América win in Paraguay in 1999.

facts.label: European move
facts.prompt: In what year did Ronaldinho leave Grêmio and sign for Paris Saint-Germain?
facts.scope: Ronaldinho’s transfer from Grêmio to Paris Saint-Germain, per FIFA’s 2018 retrospective.
facts.evidence: FIFA says he left Grêmio for Europe in 2001 and signed for PSG.

lessons.title: Ronaldinho turns the 2002 quarter-final
lessons.subtitle: A long-range free kick sent Brazil past England.

story.title: A decisive strike
story.body: In the 2002 FIFA World Cup quarter-final, England led before Rivaldo equalized. Ronaldinho then sent a free kick from more than 35 yards over David Seaman, putting Brazil ahead 2–1 and into the semi-finals.

story.title: His own explanation
story.body: The FIFA account records Ronaldinho’s explanation that he saw the goalkeeper advanced and intended to shoot, though the ball travelled higher and farther than he expected. The moment stands apart from his club career and later awards.

facts.label: Knockout stage
facts.prompt: At which 2002 FIFA World Cup knockout stage did Ronaldinho score the free kick against England?
facts.scope: Brazil–England, 2002 FIFA World Cup quarter-final.
facts.evidence: FIFA identifies Brazil’s 2–1 win over England as the 2002 World Cup quarter-final and says Ronaldinho scored the winning free kick.

facts.label: Free-kick distance
facts.prompt: From approximately how far away did Ronaldinho send Brazil’s decisive free kick over England goalkeeper David Seaman in 2002?
facts.scope: Ronaldinho’s decisive free kick in Brazil–England, 2002 World Cup quarter-final; approximate distance per FIFA.
facts.evidence: FIFA describes Ronaldinho’s free kick as coming from over 35 yards out.

facts.label: England goalkeeper
facts.prompt: Which England goalkeeper did Ronaldinho beat with Brazil’s winning free kick in the 2002 World Cup quarter-final?
facts.scope: Brazil–England, 2002 FIFA World Cup quarter-final.
facts.evidence: FIFA’s match retrospective identifies David Seaman as the goalkeeper beaten by Ronaldinho’s free kick.

lessons.title: Ronaldinho’s Barcelona match milestones
lessons.subtitle: His first league match and a decisive night in Madrid stand out in the club archive.

story.title: A debut goal
story.body: FC Barcelona’s March 2018 retrospective says Ronaldinho scored on his league debut at Camp Nou against Sevilla on 3 September 2003, cutting in from the wing and shooting beneath the crossbar.

story.title: A Madrid ovation
story.body: The same retrospective recalls the 3–0 win at Real Madrid on 19 November 2005, where Ronaldinho scored twice and received a standing ovation from the Santiago Bernabéu crowd.

facts.label: League-debut opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Ronaldinho score against on his FC Barcelona league debut at Camp Nou on 3 September 2003?
facts.scope: FC Barcelona league debut at Camp Nou, 3 September 2003; FC Barcelona March 2018 retrospective.
facts.evidence: FC Barcelona says Ronaldinho scored a goal on his league debut at Camp Nou against Sevilla.

facts.label: League-debut date
facts.prompt: On what date did Ronaldinho score on his FC Barcelona league debut at Camp Nou?
facts.scope: Ronaldinho’s FC Barcelona league debut at Camp Nou; date in club retrospective.
facts.evidence: FC Barcelona dates the debut match to 3 September 2003.

facts.label: Bernabéu brace
facts.prompt: How many goals did Ronaldinho score in FC Barcelona’s 3–0 win at Real Madrid on 19 November 2005?
facts.scope: FC Barcelona away match at Real Madrid, 19 November 2005; club retrospective.
facts.evidence: FC Barcelona states Ronaldinho scored twice in the 3–0 Bernabéu win on 19 November 2005.

lessons.title: Ronaldinho’s global honors
lessons.subtitle: His career brought individual awards and international success.

story.title: World’s best
story.body: Barcelona’s profile credits Ronaldinho with FIFA World Player awards in 2004 and 2005 and the 2005 Ballon d’Or.

story.title: A world champion
story.body: The club also lists the 2002 FIFA World Cup with Brazil among his honors.

facts.label: Ronaldinho’s FIFA World Player awards
facts.prompt: How many FIFA World Player awards did Ronaldinho earn in 2004 and 2005?
facts.scope: FIFA World Player distinction.
facts.evidence: Barcelona lists awards in 2004 and 2005.

facts.label: Ronaldinho’s Ballon d’Or year
facts.prompt: In what year did Ronaldinho win the Ballon d’Or while playing for FC Barcelona?
facts.scope: Individual award year.
facts.evidence: Barcelona lists the Ballon d’Or in 2005.

facts.label: Ronaldinho’s World Cup year
facts.prompt: In what year did Ronaldinho win the FIFA World Cup with Brazil?
facts.scope: Senior national-team honor.
facts.evidence: Barcelona lists the World Cup title with Brazil in 2002.

lessons.title: Volpi’s route between Brazil and Mexico
lessons.subtitle: A keeper’s career connects Figueirense, Querétaro and São Paulo.

story.title: A move to Mexico
story.body: Volpi joined Querétaro in 2015 after his time at Figueirense. He became captain and helped the club win its first cup honours.

story.title: A return to Brazil
story.body: São Paulo announced a one-year loan from Querétaro in December 2018 for the 2019 season. The club exercised its purchase option at the end of that year.

facts.label: Before Querétaro
facts.prompt: Which Brazilian club did Tiago Volpi leave for Querétaro after the 2014 season?
facts.scope: Volpi transfer chronology, 2014–15.
facts.evidence: São Paulo’s signing account identifies Figueirense as his club from 2012 to 2014 before Querétaro.

facts.label: Mexico arrival
facts.prompt: In which year did Tiago Volpi begin playing for Querétaro?
facts.scope: Querétaro arrival, 2015.
facts.evidence: The career list dates Querétaro to 2015–2018.

facts.label: Brazil loan
facts.prompt: Which club took Tiago Volpi on loan from Querétaro for the 2019 season?
facts.scope: December 2018 announcement for the 2019 season.
facts.evidence: São Paulo announced a one-year loan with an option to buy.

lessons.title: Volpi denies a penalty in Washington
lessons.subtitle: His save helped Querétaro close out the quarterfinal.

story.title: A first-leg cushion
story.body: Querétaro beat D.C. United 2–0 at home in the opening leg.

story.title: A crucial stop
story.body: In the return match, Volpi stopped Chris Rolfe’s penalty in the 56th minute. The 1–1 draw sent Querétaro through 3–1 on aggregate.

facts.label: Volpi’s D.C. United penalty-save date
facts.prompt: On what date did Tiago Volpi save Chris Rolfe’s penalty for Querétaro against D.C. United?
facts.scope: Quarterfinal second leg in Washington.
facts.evidence: CONCACAF dates the second leg to 1 March 2016.

facts.label: Minute of Volpi’s penalty save
facts.prompt: In which minute did Tiago Volpi save Chris Rolfe’s penalty for Querétaro against D.C. United?
facts.scope: Second leg against D.C. United.
facts.evidence: The match report records Volpi’s penalty save in the 56th minute.

facts.label: Volpi’s saves against D.C. United
facts.prompt: How many saves did Tiago Volpi make in Querétaro’s 1–1 second leg against D.C. United on 1 March 2016?
facts.scope: Quarterfinal second leg.
facts.evidence: CONCACAF reports nine saves by Volpi in the 1–1 draw.

lessons.title: Volpi’s São Paulo appearance records
lessons.subtitle: Completed club records keep their 2022 farewell date.

story.title: A completed spell
story.body: São Paulo’s May 2022 farewell records 195 appearances for Volpi. He then moved permanently to Toluca, returning to Mexican football.

story.title: Continuity in goal
